evidence: src/business/services/LendingService.ts: constructor injects `BookGateway`, `MemberGateway`, `LoanGateway` and maps records to `new Member(...)`, `new Book(...)`, `new Loan(...)` before applying rules (`member.canBorrow`, `book.checkOut`, `loan.close`).

src/business/services/LoanHistoryService.ts: `constructor(private readonly db: PrismaService)` with `db.loanEvent.create({ data: {...} })` and `this.db.loanEvent.findMany({ where: { loanId } })`: direct ORM access with no gateway.

src/business/services/LoanHistoryService.ts: `LoanEvent` is a plain interface with `kind: string`, and rows are mapped by hand. It has no domain model, unlike the Loan/Book/Member models used by LendingService.
src/business/services/LendingService.ts: `private sequence = 0; ... this.sequence += 1; `loan-${this.sequence}``: in-memory ID generation.
src/business/services/LoanHistoryService.ts: `private counter = 0; ... this.counter += 1; `evt-${this.counter}``: the same ID-generation rule written again.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files deal with loans, so the concern is roughly the same, but they don't share one abstraction or boundary. LendingService reaches storage only through injected gateways (BookGateway, MemberGateway, LoanGateway) and turns the records it gets back into domain models (Member, Book, Loan) whose methods enforce the invariants. LoanHistoryService skips that pattern. It injects PrismaService directly, calls the ORM delegate `db.loanEvent.create/findMany` itself, and works on raw rows and an untyped `kind: string`. It has no gateway and no domain model. This is the 'bypass the module's own abstractions' case: the two services persist data in inconsistent ways. The ID-generation rule is also written twice. Each service keeps its own mutable in-memory counter and builds string IDs from it (`sequence` → `loan-${n}` in LendingService, `counter` → `evt-${n}` in LoanHistoryService). That is the same rule in two places, it isn't owned by any one place, and each copy breaks across instances and restarts. Import direction is out of scope and is not judged here. The violation is that the files don't use the module's abstractions consistently.

violations.message: Skips the module's gateway and domain-model abstraction. It injects PrismaService and calls `db.loanEvent.create/findMany` directly on raw rows, while LendingService reaches storage only through Book/Member/LoanGateway and domain models.
Repeats the ID-generation rule (`private counter` → `evt-${counter}`) instead of sharing one owner with LendingService's `sequence` → `loan-${sequence}`.
Keeps its own in-memory ID sequence (`private sequence`, `loan-${this.sequence}`). LoanHistoryService has a copy of the same rule, so it doesn't live in one place.
